solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dealing with awful dread, prisoners finally render hymn maybe

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of dread are jumbled
finally picks out the closing letter of prisoners

parts.note: to render a hymn is, for example, to sing it

explanation.surface: A grim scene in which prisoners, after much dread, finally sing a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges DREAD into ADDRE; 'finally' takes the S closing 'prisoners'.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it, so dealing with a matter is tackling it.

clue.text: Sea creatures disturbing gutless lad on ship

indicators.note: disturbing means throwing into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
gutless means with the insides removed, leaving only the ends

explanation.surface: Sea creatures upsetting a timid boy aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves LD from LAD, then 'disturbing' shuffles LD, ON and SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are marine mammals, creatures of the sea.

clue.text: A final message is cut

definitions.meaning: the letters on a gravestone, short for rest in peace

explanation.surface: A final note that has been slashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rest in peace is a farewell on graves, and tearing is cutting roughly.

clue.text: Observe pair immersed in that European river

indicators.note: immersed in means sitting inside the other word

parts.note: to see is to observe

explanation.surface: Watch a couple bathing in a continental river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spree is a German river flowing through Berlin.

clue.text: Enforcer's confession of exhibitionism?

definitions.meaning: an enforcer is someone who imposes rules, with the 's meaning is
a show-off admitting the fact would say I am one who strikes a pose

explanation.surface: A bouncer owns up to liking to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M POSER, the answer is a show-off's admission.
explanation.definitionFit: One who imposes a rule or penalty enforces it, so an enforcer.

clue.text: Be opposed to having game once more on street

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the earlier piece

parts.note: Go is an Asian board game
again means once more

explanation.surface: Objecting to playing a game in the road a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To go against something is to oppose or resist it.

clue.text: Having little wriggle room, as they say, for a settlement

indicators.note: as they say signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a space with little wriggle room is packed tight

explanation.surface: A deal so tight that it leaves the parties hardly any room to manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is an agreement, and a settlement is an agreement that ends a dispute.

clue.text: Individual not getting on always munched to keep going

indicators.note: not getting means leaving out the word that follows

parts.note: a person is an individual
taken as written
ever means always
munched means ate

explanation.surface: A lone eater who never stops chomping away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting on' removes ON from PERSON, leaving PERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To perseverate is to continue or repeat something persistently.

clue.text: Yellow bird hiding under roof of cottage

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the second piece below the first
in a down clue the roof is the top, so the first letter of cottage

parts.note: a raven is a bird

explanation.surface: A yellow bird sheltering beneath a cottage roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means utterly lacking courage.

clue.text: Some friend about to roll over in bunk

indicators.note: rolling over turns the string of pieces round so it reads from the far end

parts.note: some of a thing is part of it
a pal is a friend
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A friend about to turn over in a bunk bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed, but it is short for bunkum, nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk is empty talk or nonsense, the same as hollow showy rubbish.

clue.text: An American woman far from home

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article a
broad is American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An American woman who is a long way from her own country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abroad is in a foreign country, a long way from where they live.

clue.text: Land once having little rain, hard to penetrate

indicators.note: the hard letter penetrates, going into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a trace of rain is a very small amount
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An old country so dry that its hard ground is difficult to break into.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of south-east Europe, so a land of former times.

clue.text: A talent for engaging chaps, bringing responsiveness to suggestions

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or holding the other piece

parts.note: ability is talent
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Having a gift for charming men makes someone open to ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Being amenable means readily agreeing or yielding, so it is openness to persuasion.

clue.text: Very hard worker, revolutionary type, drooled

parts.note: someone who works very hard slaves away, a slave
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A description of an exhausted labouring revolutionary who ended up dribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, the same as dribbling.

clue.text: Nice man Peter, out to show overindulgence

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter, a nice man, goes out on the town and shows how much he overdoes things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles NICE MAN PETER; 'to show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperance is lack of moderation, especially in drinking, which is overindulgence.

clue.text: Writer is upset — one departs having money but no work?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, reading the word backwards

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A writer, upset that someone has left, frets about money and work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioned person receives a regular income after retiring from employment.

clue.text: King and queen may get together in this operetta

definitions.text: King and queen may get together in this
definitions.meaning: a solitaire card game, in which court cards are built up in sequence
the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera of that name

explanation.surface: A royal couple's meeting in a light opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is laid out alone, and Gilbert and Sullivan wrote a comic opera of that name.

clue.text: Retrograde hair dye and a funny hat — style for a famous wife

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the dye is written from the end

parts.note: henna is a reddish hair dye

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of hat are mixed up

parts.note: a way of doing things is a style

explanation.surface: A wife with dyed hair and an odd hat dressing in her own style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' turns HENNA into ANNEH; A is as printed and 'funny' turns HAT into THA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Hathaway was the wife of William Shakespeare, famous through her husband.

clue.text: Meat back in short supply — only a comedian would eat it?!

definitions.text: only a comedian would eat it?!

parts.note: ham is meat

indicators.note: the stern being in short supply means it is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Meat is scarce again, so only a comic would eat this.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the British tabloid headline 'Freddie Starr ate my hamster' about the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pet rodent, famously said by a tabloid to have been eaten by a comic.

clue.text: Alpine ground for one in mountainous territory

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alpine ground serving for someone living in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpine' tempts towards Switzerland but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Nepal, a Himalayan country, lives in a mountainous land.

clue.text: Raving dean's foremost priest, one into drink

indicators.note: foremost picks the leading letter of dean's

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rum is a drink
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean's senior priest is drunk and rambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium is a disturbed state of mind marked by wild talk, so raving is a fair description.

clue.text: Kills female animal — wicked act

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: A hunter kills a female deer, which is a wicked deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone in is an informal phrase meaning to murder them.

clue.text: Study this writer's material

parts.note: a den is a private study room
the setter is this writer, so this writer is I am, or I'M

explanation.surface: Study what I am made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Number one hit going around country

indicators.note: going around turns the run of pieces back to front

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to tan is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A chart-topping hit song travelling round the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one hit' reads as a chart-topper but splits into number, one and hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a country, a people under one government.

clue.text: Hint of something has Heather getting into a twist

parts.note: a tang is a slight trace or taste of something
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone called Heather gets flustered at a hint of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into a twist means becoming knotted or snarled, as string does.

clue.text: Fate of man married to backward-looking woman

definitions.meaning: one's fortune or destiny in life
in Genesis his wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: The destiny of a man whose wife keeps looking behind her.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's lot is their destiny, and the biblical figure's wife looked back.

clue.text: Light railway next to main road

indicators.note: next to puts one piece beside the other

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered main road, written AI

explanation.surface: A light railway line running alongside a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is open and full of light, so light describes it well.

clue.text: Evil affair — stuff we can't see

parts.note: dark deeds are evil ones
a matter is an affair or business

explanation.surface: A wicked business that is kept hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists' dark matter is invisible material inferred only from its gravity.
